rules.rationale: Source ESOL prior for smiles_short was +6.89 (n=261); small solutes pay little cavity-formation cost.
Source smiles_mid effect was -6.61 (n=226); transferred with damping because role confidence is only 0.22.
Strongest source value prior (-11.46, confidence 0.47): bulky lipophilic solutes lose solvation favorability.
Donor-to-heteroatom role transfer is weakest evidence (confidence 0.16), so polarity enters only as a small positive tilt.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the ESOL size ordering (short favored, mid and long penalized) with a small heteroatom tilt, letting the target-only anchor dominate late. Fails if hydration rewards large polar solutes.

rules.rationale: Cavity formation scales with solute volume; compact solutes retain the most favorable hydration balance.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the lowest-confidence source role (0.16), since heteroatom-dense solutes here are also large.
Polyhalogenated solutes are weakly hydrogen bonding and bulky, a classic hydrophobic hydration penalty.
Extended chains add nonpolar surface faster than polar contacts, reducing hydration favorability.

skills.hypothesis: Size and hydrophobic surface, not heteroatom density, set hydration ranking; the uncertain donor-to-heteroatom role is reversed. Fails if polar multi-heteroatom solutes actually top the score.

state.lesson: On development seeds the source-prior length skill led the heteroatom-led mechanistic skill by roughly 23 AUC points, so size priors plus lighter semantic mass are the safer carrier; heteroatom weighting should stay small until target evidence accumulates.
state.revision_summary: Kept the better-performing source-prior transfer but damped the heteroatom rule and reduced semantic mass and prior scale so the target-only anchor takes over sooner. Replaced the losing polarity-led skill with a compact-apolar counter-hypothesis that explicitly reverses the lowest-confidence donor-to-heteroatom role while retaining size and halogen terms. Selected the damped length-prior transfer for frozen deployment.
